claims.text: Inverse-model-guided selection under high-alkalinity, moderate-temperature synthesis will induce beneficial Cu–Pt electronic cooperation.
The proposed synthesis and selection strategy will minimize deactivating Pt–Ni/Fe interactions.
The proposed synthesis and selection strategy will enhance redox buffering.
The resulting catalyst will improve low-temperature hydrocarbon oxidation and NO reduction after severe ageing relative to Pd/Al2O3.
The initial catalysts have a total metal loading of 1 wt% and contain up to 19 metal precursors supported on La-doped gamma-Al2O3.
The fresh initial catalysts contain agglomerates of fine metallic particles.
The intervention uses automated continuous-solvothermal synthesis at 200–350 °C and 20–35 MPa with 25 M NaOH.
Machine learning and Bayesian optimization will select compositions enriched in metals such as Pd, Rh, and Ga using post-ageing activity screening.
Controlled high-alkalinity synthesis facilitates post-ageing reconstruction into electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative adsorption sites.
Controlled high-alkalinity synthesis reduces formation of Pt–Ni/Fe species and preserves beneficial alloy/support interfacial states.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites weaken overly strong CO binding.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites enhance redox buffering and oxygen mobility.
Enhanced redox buffering and oxygen mobility increase i-C5H12 oxidation and NO reduction.
Pt–Ni/Fe interactions can isolate Pt and suppress its catalytic activity.
After ageing, selected catalysts will exhibit at least a 5 °C lower T50 or at least a 2 percentage-point higher conversion at 350 °C than Pd/Al2O3.
The stated operating boundary includes ageing at 900 °C for 5 hours under cyclic lean/rich conditions with H2O, followed by oxidation and reduction at 500 °C.
The activity test uses a 100–500 °C near-stoichiometric feed containing 500 ppm NO, 5000 ppm CO, 200 ppm C3H6, and 120 ppm i-C5H12.
CO-adsorption FT-IR and HAADF-STEM/EDS can test for the proposed electronic coupling and elemental segregation.
